sets.title: Ward & medicines policy extracts
sets.instruction: Six workplace extracts. Choose A, B or C. Focus phrases highlighted.

items.extract:
From the Trust medicines reconciliation policy:

Medicines reconciliation must be completed within 24 hours of admission for all adult inpatients, and sooner if the patient is critically ill or on high-risk medicines (anticoagulants, insulin, anticonvulsants, transplant immunosuppression). Discrepancies between the patient’s reported list, blister packs, and the electronic record should be clarified with the usual GP or community pharmacy before discharge prescribing is finalised. Do not rely on a previous discharge letter alone. Document every source used, including what could not be verified. If reconciliation is incomplete at the time of transfer between wards or to another hospital, the receiving team must be informed explicitly in the verbal handover, not only via an unreadable note buried in the record. Incomplete reconciliation is a clinical risk, not an administrative inconvenience. Pharmacy technicians may gather the history, but the final reconciled list must be checked and signed by a prescriber or pharmacist. Where the patient manages their own medicines, ask to see the containers rather than accepting a verbal list.
items.stem: The policy mainly requires staff to

options.text: accept the most recent discharge letter as the definitive list of medicines.
obtain a full medicines history from the GP before any drug is prescribed.
complete reconciliation early and communicate any unresolved gaps at handover.

items.explain: 핵심: complete reconciliation early and communicate any unresolved gaps at handover.

items.extract:
Email from the endoscopy lead to all referrers:

Please stop sending ‘urgent’ booking requests without stating the clinical indication, relevant blood results, anticoagulation/antiplatelet status, and whether the patient needs an interpreter. Incomplete forms are returned to the referrer, which delays the very patients you are trying to prioritise. If the case is truly unstable, discuss directly with the on-call endoscopist rather than using the routine e-form pathway. Remember that labelling every request urgent destroys our ability to triage real bleeding and obstruction. Incomplete urgency is not kindness; it is hidden delay. A request that arrives complete at 4 p.m. will usually be booked faster than an incomplete one sent at 9 a.m., because the second must wait to be returned, corrected and resubmitted.
items.stem: The lead’s main concern is that

options.text: incomplete referral forms are themselves a source of delay.
referrers are booking stable patients through the on-call endoscopist.
interpreters are not being arranged for urgent procedures.

items.explain: 핵심: incomplete referral forms are themselves a source of delay.

items.extract:
Nursing handover note (afternoon):

Mrs Lee’s NEWS2 has risen from 3 to 6 since midday, mainly due to respiratory rate 28 and new confusion. Blood pressure is ⁹⁸/60 with cool peripheries. Oxygen started at 2 L via nasal cannulae per protocol targeting SpO₂ 94–98%. Medical review requested at 14:10; not yet seen. Family updated that she is more sleepy than this morning. Please escalate again if NEWS2 rises further or urine output remains <20 mL/h. Sepsis pathway considered — cultures taken; awaiting first antibiotic dose confirmation from doctor. Her son has asked to be telephoned if she is moved to a higher level of care; his number is on the front sheet.
items.stem: The note indicates that

options.text: oxygen was started because the family reported increased sleepiness.
a medical review has been requested but has not yet taken place.
the sepsis pathway has been completed and the first antibiotic dose has already been given.

items.explain: 핵심: a medical review has been requested but has not yet taken place.

items.extract:
Pharmacy bulletin — modified-release medicines:

Do not crush modified-release metformin tablets or other MR/SR/XL preparations unless pharmacy has confirmed a crushable alternative. Crushing can cause dose dumping and toxicity. If a patient cannot swallow solids, contact pharmacy the same day for an appropriate liquid, dispersible, or alternative drug. Document the swallowing problem on the chart. Ward stock of covert medication thickeners does not make crushing MR metformin acceptable. When in doubt, withhold the dose and obtain advice rather than improvising a dangerous workaround. Where a modified-release product has been prescribed only for the convenience of once-daily dosing, an immediate-release equivalent given more frequently is often the simplest solution.
items.stem: Staff are advised to

options.text: withhold metformin until the patient is able to swallow solids again.
seek an alternative formulation from pharmacy rather than crush the tablet.
use thickener so that modified-release tablets can be crushed safely.

items.explain: 핵심: seek an alternative formulation from pharmacy rather than crush the tablet.

items.extract:
Occupational health memo — measles exposure:

Staff with unprotected exposure to measles should contact Occupational Health the same day, even if they believe their immunisation history is complete. Exclusion advice depends on documented immunity evidence (two MMR doses or positive serology), not on job title or years of service. Do not wait until the next shift if exposure occurred today. Agency staff must use the same pathway. Managers should release staff to attend OH promptly; delaying assessment increases risk to vulnerable patients on the ward. Those found to be non-immune may be offered post-exposure MMR or immunoglobulin depending on timing, so the sooner the call is made the more options remain.
items.stem: According to the memo,

options.text: agency staff should follow their own agency’s exposure pathway.
staff who can show two documented MMR doses do not need to contact Occupational Health at all.
staff must contact Occupational Health on the day of exposure regardless of their vaccination history.

items.explain: 핵심: staff must contact Occupational Health on the day of exposure regardless of their vaccination history.

items.extract:
Discharge checklist reminder (all wards):

Confirm follow-up appointments are booked and communicated before the patient leaves the ward. ‘To be arranged by GP’ is acceptable only when the receiving practice has already acknowledged the request in writing (email/EHR task). Give patients a written safety-net sheet listing red flags and a contact number that works after 5 p.m. Check that high-risk medicines have a clear restart plan. A bed empty without these steps is not a successful discharge; it is a deferred failure that will return through the emergency department. Where transport is delayed, use the waiting time to complete these items rather than treating the discharge lounge as the end of ward responsibility.
items.stem: The reminder stresses that

options.text: follow-up must be confirmed, and GP arrangements acknowledged in writing, before discharge.
patients should be given a contact number for the ward that is staffed overnight.
discharges should be delayed until a GP appointment date is known.

items.explain: 핵심: follow-up must be confirmed, and GP arrangements acknowledged in writing, before discharge.

gist: Part B = purpose of extract; underline verbs must/do not/contact.

sets.title: Theatre, IPC & governance extracts
sets.instruction: Six extracts · 3 options. Focus phrases highlighted.

items.extract:
Pre-operative assessment guidance — SGLT2 inhibitors:

Patients on SGLT2 inhibitors (e.g. dapagliflozin, empagliflozin) should usually omit the dose on the day of surgery. For prolonged fasting, bowel prep, or higher-risk procedures, omit the day before as well. Restart when eating and drinking normally, typically 24–48 hours post-op if renal function and hydration are acceptable. Suspect euglycaemic ketoacidosis if unexplained acidosis, nausea, or tachypnoea occurs peri-operatively — check ketones even if glucose is not very high. If unsure, confirm the plan with the anaesthetist named on the list rather than guessing from an old letter. Patients should be told the reason for the omission and given a written restart date, as many will otherwise resume the drug on the evening of surgery.
items.stem: The guidance mainly tells staff to

options.text: check ketones only when glucose is markedly elevated.
omit peri-operative doses as described and confirm the plan with the anaesthetist if unsure.
stop SGLT2 inhibitors at least 48 hours before every surgical procedure regardless of its duration.

items.explain: 핵심: omit peri-operative doses as described and confirm the plan with the anaesthetist if unsure.

items.extract:
Infection control update — aerosol-generating procedures (AGPs):

Visors alone are not a substitute for a fluid-resistant surgical mask during AGPs. Both an appropriate mask and eye protection are required unless a higher-specification respirator is indicated by local risk assessment. Fit-testing must be in date for respirator use. Donning and doffing remain common failure points; buddy checks are encouraged for unfamiliar staff. PPE shortages do not authorise improvisation that leaves the airway unprotected. If stock is constrained, escalate to the IPC team rather than downgrading protection silently on the ward. Staff who have not been fit-tested within the required interval should be redeployed from AGP duties until this is completed.
items.stem: The update clarifies that

options.text: a visor cannot be used instead of a mask during aerosol-generating procedures.
eye protection may be omitted whenever a fit-tested respirator is worn for the procedure.
a respirator is required for all aerosol-generating procedures.

items.explain: 핵심: a visor cannot be used instead of a mask during aerosol-generating procedures.

items.extract:
Outpatient letter standard operating procedure:

Copy patients into clinic letters by default unless they have opted out. Write so that a non-specialist adult can follow the plan: avoid unexplained abbreviations, state what will happen next, and list actions for the GP versus actions for the patient. If bad news was discussed, ensure the letter matches what was said in the room. Letters are part of the clinical record and part of the relationship. A technically correct letter that the patient cannot understand is an incomplete clinical task. Where an interpreter was used in clinic, state this in the letter and consider whether a translated summary is needed.
items.stem: Authors of clinic letters should

options.text: copy in patients only when bad news has been discussed.
send patients a separate simplified version of the letter written for the GP.
copy patients in by default and write in language a non-specialist can follow.

items.explain: 핵심: copy patients in by default and write in language a non-specialist can follow.

items.extract:
Blood transfusion bedside checklist:

Two trained staff must check identity at the bedside immediately before transfusion begins, using open questions and matching wristband, prescription, and unit label. Checking in a corridor or treatment room without the patient present is not acceptable. If any element does not match, stop and contact blood bank — do not ‘correct’ labels on the ward. Remain with the patient for the first 15 minutes of each unit. Document start time, observations, and any reaction. Speed of setup never justifies skipping the final bedside check. Emergency O-negative units are checked in the same way; the urgency of the situation changes the speed of the check, not its content.
items.stem: The checklist emphasises that identity checks must be

options.text: repeated every 15 minutes during the transfusion.
completed in the treatment room by two staff before the unit is brought to the patient.
done by two trained staff at the bedside immediately before the unit is started.

items.explain: 핵심: done by two trained staff at the bedside immediately before the unit is started.

items.extract:
Falls prevention brief for night staff:

A completed falls risk score does not replace continuous clinical observation. If a patient becomes newly restless, tries to climb out of bed, or repeatedly calls for the toilet, escalate promptly even if the morning score was low. Consider toileting schedules, continence support, medication review for sedatives, and whether enhanced supervision is needed. Document what you saw, not only the score. Families’ warnings that ‘this is how it started last time’ should be treated as clinical data. Scores help triage; they do not freeze risk for the next twelve hours. Night sedation given for the first time in hospital is a particular trigger; review whether it is needed before administering it.
items.stem: The brief warns that

options.text: falls risk scores should be repeated every twelve hours overnight.
a change in behaviour requires escalation even when the recorded risk score is low.
family concerns should be documented but not acted upon until a doctor has reviewed the patient.

items.explain: 핵심: a change in behaviour requires escalation even when the recorded risk score is low.

items.extract:
Research governance note — consent for studies:

Staff may discuss a study with potentially eligible patients and provide approved information sheets, but must not obtain consent unless they are named on the delegation log and have completed the required training. Consent taken by unauthorised staff is invalid and may halt the study. If a patient asks detailed medical questions beyond your role, involve the principal investigator or delegated clinician. Document discussions. Enthusiasm for recruitment is welcome; shortcuts around governance are not. If a patient expresses interest outside working hours, record their contact details and pass them to the research team rather than attempting the process yourself.
items.stem: According to the note, consent may be taken only by staff who

options.text: are named on the delegation log and have completed the required training.
have discussed the study with the patient and provided the information sheet.
are supervised by the principal investigator during the consent discussion.

items.explain: 핵심: are named on the delegation log and have completed the required training.

gist: Find the rule and the exception.

sets.title: Emergency department & radiology extracts
sets.instruction: Six workplace extracts. Choose A, B or C. Focus phrases highlighted.

items.extract:
Extract from the radiology department contrast media allergy policy:

All patients must be screened for prior adverse reactions to iodinated contrast media at the time of referral. Patients who have experienced a prior moderate or severe reaction — defined as bronchospasm, laryngeal oedema, or any reaction requiring emergency treatment — must receive a corticosteroid pre-medication protocol (methylprednisolone 32 mg orally at 12 hours and 2 hours before contrast administration) and must not proceed without an anaesthetist informed and available. A low-osmolality, non-ionic agent must be used in all cases of prior reaction, regardless of severity. Patients with mild prior reactions such as urticaria, flushing, or limited pruritus may proceed after a risk–benefit discussion documented by the reporting radiologist. Renal function must be checked within 72 hours of any contrast-enhanced CT in patients prescribed metformin or with an estimated GFR below 45 mL/min/1.73 m². Record all decisions in the radiology information system before the patient enters the scan room.
items.stem: According to the policy, patients who have experienced a prior moderate or severe contrast reaction must

options.text: use a low-osmolality, non-ionic agent and arrange a documented risk–benefit discussion with the reporting radiologist before the scan.
have renal function checked within 72 hours and be reviewed by an anaesthetist to confirm they are safe to receive contrast.
receive the corticosteroid pre-medication protocol and not proceed until an anaesthetist has been informed and is available.

items.explain: 핵심: prior moderate or severe reaction → pre-medication protocol AND anaesthetist informed and available before proceeding.

items.extract:
Memo from the ED clinical lead to all triage nursing staff:

It has come to my attention that triage timestamps are not always being entered at the actual moment of patient assessment. Entering the time retrospectively — even by a few minutes — distorts our four-hour performance data and, more seriously, masks real delays in identifying high-acuity patients. From Monday, all nurses must log the triage timestamp at the point of face-to-face assessment, not on return from a cubicle or at end of shift. If the electronic system is temporarily unavailable, record the time on the paper triage card immediately and transfer it to the system as soon as access is restored, noting any discrepancy. Persistent retrospective entry will be treated as a documentation breach and managed through the Trust's conduct procedure. Please discuss any system-access difficulties with your shift coordinator rather than working around them.
items.stem: The memo mainly tells triage nurses to

options.text: record the triage time at the point of face-to-face assessment and not enter it retrospectively.
report any patient waiting more than four hours directly to the clinical lead before the end of their shift.
contact the shift coordinator whenever they encounter difficulties accessing the electronic triage system.

items.explain: 핵심: log the triage timestamp at the point of face-to-face assessment — not retrospectively.

items.extract:
Notice from the Radiation Protection Supervisor — mandatory reading for all emergency department staff:

All clinical staff working in areas where ionising radiation is used must hold a current radiation awareness certificate. This certificate must be renewed every three years. Certificates obtained through external providers are acceptable only if the course content has been pre-approved by the Trust Radiation Protection Adviser. Staff without a valid certificate may not enter a controlled radiation area while a procedure is in progress, even if accompanied by a certificated colleague. Temporary or locum staff must provide evidence of a valid certificate before commencing duties in the department. Line managers are responsible for confirming compliance before a new member of staff begins work in a radiation area. Do not assume that completing the Trust induction covers this requirement — the radiation awareness certificate is a separate, mandatory qualification with its own renewal cycle.
items.stem: The purpose of this notice is to

options.text: inform staff that they may enter controlled radiation areas freely provided they are accompanied by a colleague who holds a current certificate.
remind staff that a valid radiation awareness certificate must be held, renewed every three years, and is a requirement separate from Trust induction.
require line managers to obtain radiation awareness certificates on behalf of any new staff member before those staff are permitted to start.

items.explain: 핵심: current radiation awareness certificate — renewed every three years — separate, mandatory qualification distinct from Trust induction.

items.extract:
Extract from the emergency department CT head referral guideline (adapted from NICE Head Injury guidance):

A CT scan of the head is indicated within one hour of the decision to scan if the patient has any of the following: GCS below 13 at any point since injury; GCS 13 or 14 at two hours post-injury; suspected open or depressed skull fracture; signs of basal skull fracture (haemotympanum, periorbital bruising, cerebrospinal fluid from ear or nose, or Battle's sign); post-traumatic seizure with no prior seizure history; focal neurological deficit; or more than one episode of vomiting. In patients aged 65 or older, amnesia for events more than 30 minutes before impact is sufficient to trigger immediate scanning. Anticoagulant therapy is an additional independent indication for immediate CT regardless of GCS. Do not use plain skull X-ray as a substitute for CT in any patient meeting these criteria. Document the time of scan request in the medical record.
items.stem: The guideline states that

options.text: patients aged 65 and over require CT only when their GCS has fallen below 13, not merely because of post-traumatic amnesia of any duration.
a plain skull X-ray may be used as an interim investigation before CT in patients whose GCS has remained 14 or above and who have no other high-risk features.
anticoagulant therapy alone is an independent indication for immediate CT scanning regardless of the patient's conscious level.

items.explain: 핵심: Anticoagulant therapy → immediate CT regardless of GCS; skull X-ray must not be used as a substitute.

items.extract:
ED to radiology handover note — Mr Okafor, cubicle 7:

Mr Okafor is a 71-year-old gentleman referred for urgent CT pulmonary angiography to exclude pulmonary embolism. Wells score 6 (high probability); D-dimer 4.1 µg/mL. He is prescribed apixaban 5 mg twice daily; last dose taken this morning. Observations: blood pressure 94/60 mmHg, heart rate 116 bpm, SpO₂ 86% on 6 L oxygen via face mask. He has a documented iodinated contrast allergy (urticaria in 2019); oral pre-medication was not given due to clinical urgency, and the ED registrar has accepted responsibility with written documentation in the notes. IV access is secured in the right antecubital fossa. Please ensure the radiologist is aware of the contrast allergy before proceeding and that the anaesthetic team is on standby. Results and images are required in the emergency department immediately.
items.stem: The note indicates that

options.text: pre-medication was omitted due to clinical urgency, so the radiologist must be warned of the contrast allergy before scanning proceeds.
the anaesthetic team administered the pre-medication protocol before transfer and will supervise the procedure at the scanner to manage any adverse reaction.
the ED registrar will personally accompany Mr Okafor to the scanner and accept clinical responsibility for the contrast decision on site.

items.explain: 핵심: pre-medication was not given due to clinical urgency — contrast allergy must be communicated — anaesthetic team on standby.
focusPhrases: pre-medication was not given due to clinical urgency

items.extract:
Extract from the emergency department sepsis screening standard operating procedure:

All patients presenting to the emergency department must be screened for sepsis using the National Early Warning Score 2 at the point of triage. Where NEWS2 is 5 or above, or where the triage nurse suspects an infective source, the sepsis screening tool must be completed within 15 minutes and a senior clinician notified without delay. Do not wait for laboratory results before commencing the sepsis bundle. The first dose of antibiotics must be administered within one hour of the sepsis alert being raised, irrespective of whether all blood cultures have been collected. Where a blood culture cannot be taken without causing undue delay to antibiotic administration, give antibiotics first and document the reason clearly in the medical record. Antibiotic choice must follow the Trust empirical therapy guide for the suspected source, available at each workstation and on the intranet.
items.stem: The SOP states that

options.text: blood cultures must always be obtained before any antibiotic is given, even in patients for whom taking cultures would cause undue delay.
antibiotics must be given within one hour of the sepsis alert being raised, irrespective of whether blood cultures have been taken.
the senior clinician must complete the sepsis screening tool before the triage nurse raises the alert or notifies anyone.

items.explain: 핵심: antibiotics within one hour of the sepsis alert — irrespective of whether all blood cultures collected — give antibiotics first if cultures would delay.
focusPhrases: within one hour of the sepsis alert
irrespective of whether all blood cultures

gist: Part B = purpose or main point of a short workplace text; watch must / do not / unless / irrespective.
Distractors often reverse a key condition (e.g. 'cultures before antibiotics') or misattribute a rule to the wrong staff group.
Focus phrases carry the answer — locate them in the text first, then read the surrounding sentence carefully.

sets.title: Paediatric ward & safeguarding extracts
sets.instruction: Six workplace extracts. Choose A, B or C. Focus phrases highlighted.

items.extract:
Memo from the paediatric pharmacy team to all prescribers:

All paediatric prescriptions must use an actual body weight recorded on the day of prescribing, not an estimated, age-based, or previously documented weight. Estimated weights derived from formulae (e.g. (age + 4) × 2) are acceptable only during emergency resuscitation when weighing is not possible, and this must be documented clearly with the reason. Once the child is stable, the prescription must be reviewed against the measured weight and adjusted if necessary. For children weighing more than 50 kg, adult doses apply for most drugs; consult the BNFc or ward pharmacist if uncertain. Always calculate the dose in mg/kg, write the total dose in milligrams, and verify it against the maximum adult dose. High-risk medicines — including morphine, gentamicin, and anticonvulsants — require an independent double-check by a second prescriber before administration. Record the weight in kilograms on the drug chart at the time of prescribing.
items.stem: The memo mainly tells staff to

options.text: use an age-based formula to estimate weight whenever the child is too unwell to be weighed accurately.
ask pharmacy to prescribe all high-alert drugs independently rather than calculating doses on the ward.
base all prescriptions on the actual measured weight and check each dose against the maximum adult dose.

items.explain: 핵심: base all prescriptions on the actual measured weight and check each dose against the maximum adult dose.

items.extract:
Extract from the Trust safeguarding children policy:

Any member of staff who is concerned that a child may be at risk of significant harm must make a referral to Children's Social Care, or discuss the concern with the named nurse for safeguarding, on the same working day. Do not delay a referral because a parent or carer has withheld consent; parental consent is not required when the referral is made on child protection grounds. Record all concerns in the clinical notes contemporaneously, including the name of the professional consulted and the outcome of that discussion. If a referral is made by telephone, follow it up in writing to Children's Social Care within 48 hours. Concerns about fabricated or induced illness, unexplained bruising in pre-mobile children, or repeated presentations with injuries inconsistent with the history must always be escalated directly to the named consultant for safeguarding, not managed in professional isolation. All conversations with families about referral intentions must be documented.
items.stem: According to the policy, staff who have concerns about a child's safety must

options.text: refer to Children's Social Care or consult the named nurse on the same day, even without parental consent.
obtain a senior clinician's written agreement before contacting Children's Social Care about any safeguarding concern.
delay the referral until a parent or carer has had the opportunity to provide a full explanation.

items.explain: 핵심: refer to Children's Social Care or consult the named nurse on the same day, even without parental consent.

items.extract:
Notice to all nursing and medical staff — paediatric unit:

Parents and carers are welcome to remain with their child during all clinical procedures, including venepuncture, cannulation, and lumbar puncture, unless their presence is judged by the clinical team to pose a direct risk to the safe conduct of the procedure. Offering parental presence is now a Trust standard, not an optional courtesy. Staff must offer the option before any procedure begins and document whether the parent or carer chose to stay or leave. Where a parent becomes distressed or physically interferes with the procedure, they may be asked to step outside briefly; this must be explained calmly and the parent invited to return as soon as possible. Children who have attained Fraser competence may make their own decision about whether a parent is present. Compelling a child to accept parental presence against their clearly expressed wishes is a violation of their autonomy and must never occur.
items.stem: The purpose of this notice is to

options.text: remind staff that parents must withdraw from the room during all invasive procedures to prevent procedural distress.
inform staff that offering parental presence during procedures is a Trust standard rather than a discretionary favour.
explain that parents who become upset during a procedure may be permanently excluded from the clinical area.

items.explain: 핵심: offering parental presence during procedures is a Trust standard rather than a discretionary favour.

items.extract:
Extract from the paediatric intravenous fluid prescribing guideline:

For maintenance fluid prescribing in children over 28 days and under 18 years, use a 0.9% sodium chloride with 5% glucose preparation unless a specific electrolyte abnormality requires an alternative. Calculate the daily maintenance volume using the Holliday-Segar formula: 100 mL/kg for the first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg for the next 10 kg, and 20 mL/kg for each kilogram thereafter. Do not prescribe hypotonic fluids (sodium concentration below 131 mmol/L) as routine maintenance in hospital, as these carry a recognised risk of iatrogenic hyponatraemia. Reassess fluid balance at least every 12 hours and adjust the rate for clinical changes such as pyrexia, vomiting, or ongoing surgical losses. Any child receiving intravenous fluids for more than 48 hours requires serum electrolytes checked at least twice daily. Fluid boluses for resuscitation are prescribed separately and must not be included in maintenance volume calculations.
items.stem: The guideline states that

options.text: hypotonic fluids should be prescribed whenever a child has a documented sodium abnormality on admission.
serum electrolytes must be checked daily for all children who are receiving any form of intravenous fluid.
maintenance fluids must be isotonic and fluid balance must be formally reassessed at least every 12 hours.

items.explain: 핵심: maintenance fluids must be isotonic and fluid balance must be formally reassessed at least every 12 hours.

items.extract:
Standard operating procedure — referral to the hospital play specialist service:

All children admitted for a planned procedure or with an anticipated inpatient stay of more than 48 hours should be referred to the play specialist service within 24 hours of admission. Referrals must be submitted via the electronic patient record using the 'Therapies Referral' form; verbal-only referrals will not be actioned. Indicate the primary concern on the form — procedural anxiety, needle phobia, developmental regression, or preparation for surgery — as this determines the triage priority of the response. Play specialists provide preparation for anaesthesia, distraction during clinical procedures, and environmental normalisation for long-stay children. Do not wait until the day before a procedure to submit a referral; adequate preparation requires at least two dedicated sessions for most children. The service does not cover unplanned emergency admissions as routine, but out-of-hours support may be requested by the nurse in charge where the child's distress is compromising safe care.
items.stem: The SOP mainly requires staff to

options.text: arrange play specialist input verbally through the nurse in charge for all children undergoing planned procedures.
refer eligible children via the electronic form within 24 hours of admission, stating the reason for referral.
restrict referrals to children with needle phobia who are scheduled for procedures requiring general anaesthesia.

items.explain: 핵심: refer eligible children via the electronic form within 24 hours of admission, stating the reason for referral.

items.extract:
Nursing handover note — paediatric ward, morning shift:

Joshua, 4 years, was admitted overnight with suspected non-accidental injury. The safeguarding team was notified at 22:00; the named nurse and consultant review is scheduled for 09:30 this morning. Joshua is currently comfortable, tolerating oral fluids and breakfast. His mother is present and has been informed that a social worker will attend today; his father has not visited. Do not permit any visitors other than Joshua's named mother unless the nurse in charge has approved the visit in writing following discussion with the safeguarding nurse. The police have been informed of the admission. A multidisciplinary X-ray review meeting is scheduled at 11:00 — both the ward registrar and named safeguarding consultant must attend. Clinical photographs of the injuries have been taken in accordance with the Trust safeguarding photography protocol and uploaded to the medical records system.
items.stem: The note indicates that

options.text: visiting access to this child has been restricted and only his named mother is currently permitted.
the social worker has already spoken to Joshua's father and agreed a safeguarding plan overnight.
the safeguarding team was first contacted this morning following a ward round assessment of the injuries.

items.explain: 핵심: visiting access to this child has been restricted and only his named mother is currently permitted.

gist: Part B = main point or required action of a short workplace text; watch for must / do not / unless / only.

sets.instruction: Six workplace extracts. Choose A, B or C. Focus phrases highlighted.

items.extract:
Extract from the maternity CTG escalation policy:

All midwives must document a fresh CTG assessment at the start of every shift and whenever there is a clinical concern. A CTG classified as pathological under the current NICE criteria requires immediate medical review by the registrar or above; do not wait until the end of the current hour block. If the registrar is not immediately available, the bleep must be escalated to the consultant within five minutes. Failure to escalate a pathological CTG is a never event under local policy. Maternal repositioning, IV fluid bolus, and cessation of oxytocin should be initiated simultaneously whilst awaiting the doctor. Document the time of every escalation attempt in the maternity records and on the CTG paper. A suspicious CTG warrants an earlier review than the routine one-hour interval; use clinical judgement to determine the safe monitoring interval, which must be recorded.
items.stem: The policy mainly requires midwives to

options.text: escalate a pathological CTG to a registrar without delay and document every step taken.
reclassify a suspicious CTG as pathological before requesting any medical review.
withhold oxytocin infusions whenever a CTG is classified as suspicious or pathological.

items.explain: 핵심: pathological CTG requires immediate medical review; document every escalation attempt.

items.extract:
Memo from the labour ward coordinator to all midwifery staff:

Following last month's postpartum haemorrhage (PPH) drill, several gaps were identified in the team's preparation. From this week, the PPH emergency box will be checked and signed off at the beginning of every early and late shift. The box must contain: two large-bore IV cannulae, one litre bags of 0.9% saline, cross-match bottles, the PPH drug tray including oxytocin 10 IU IM and ergometrine, and a laminated PPH algorithm. Any items found missing must be replaced before the shift handover is complete. The maternity support worker may restock consumables but a registered midwife must countersign the checklist. Drills will be repeated quarterly; attendance is mandatory for all band 5–7 staff. Please direct questions to the lead midwife, not to the labour ward coordinator.
items.stem: The memo tells staff that

options.text: PPH drills replace the need for a signed equipment check at the start of each shift.
the emergency box must be checked and signed by a registered midwife at every shift start.
a maternity support worker may countersign the checklist if the registered midwife is unavailable.

items.explain: 핵심: PPH box must be checked and countersigned by a registered midwife at every shift start.

items.extract:
Extract from the neonatal unit hypoglycaemia guideline:

Neonates at risk of hypoglycaemia (infants of diabetic mothers, those born before 37 weeks, birth weight below 2.5 kg or above 4.5 kg, and those with clinical signs) should have a blood glucose checked within 2–4 hours of birth and before feeds thereafter. A blood glucose below 2.0 mmol/L in any neonate requires immediate intervention: feed the infant if able and recheck within 30 minutes. If the repeat value remains below 2.0 mmol/L, or if the infant cannot feed, commence IV dextrose 10% at 60 mL/kg/day and notify the neonatal registrar immediately. Do not delay IV access to attempt a further feed. A value of 2.0–2.5 mmol/L is borderline; increase feeding frequency and recheck within one hour. Values consistently above 2.6 mmol/L in a well term neonate without risk factors do not require further screening.
items.stem: According to the guideline, when a neonate's blood glucose is below 2.0 mmol/L,

options.text: staff should attempt two further feeds before starting IV dextrose and contacting the registrar.
IV dextrose 10% must be commenced without delay, and oral feeding is contraindicated at that threshold.
a feed should be offered and a recheck performed; IV dextrose is started only if the level remains low or feeding is not possible.

items.explain: 핵심: feed if able and recheck within 30 minutes; IV dextrose only if repeat remains low or infant cannot feed.

items.extract:
Notice on the postnatal ward breastfeeding support board:

The infant feeding team is available Monday to Friday 08:00–18:00 and can be contacted via the ward bleep. Outside these hours, the duty midwife is the first point of contact for breastfeeding concerns. Do not refer mothers directly to the community lactation consultant during the inpatient stay; referrals must go through the infant feeding lead. Mothers who are experiencing nipple pain, poor latch, or concerns about milk supply should be seen before their next scheduled feed, not at the following day's ward round. Skin-to-skin contact and rooming-in are encouraged for all mother-infant pairs unless there is a clinical reason documented in the notes. Supplementary formula in the first 72 hours should only be given after a documented informed-consent discussion and must be recorded in the feeding chart. Partners and support persons are welcome to attend feeding assessments.
items.stem: The notice indicates that

options.text: mothers with breastfeeding difficulties should be reviewed before their next feed, not at the ward round.
supplementary formula may be given at the mother's request within the first 72 hours without further discussion.
mothers may contact the community lactation consultant directly during their inpatient stay.

items.explain: 핵심: mothers with concerns should be seen before their next scheduled feed, not at the following day's ward round.
focusPhrases: not at the following day's ward round

items.extract:
Extract from the maternity VTE prophylaxis standard operating procedure:

All women admitted to the maternity unit must have a VTE risk assessment completed within four hours of admission using the approved Trust tool. The assessment must be reviewed and updated following delivery, at 24 hours post-delivery, and at any change in clinical condition. Women with a score of 2 or above are eligible for pharmacological prophylaxis; prescribe low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) unless contraindicated. LMWH must not be prescribed within 12 hours of regional anaesthesia insertion or removal. Women who decline prophylaxis must have the risks explained and a declined consent form completed and filed in the maternity records. Antiembolic stockings should be offered to all women where pharmacological prophylaxis is contraindicated or declined. The prescribing midwife must alert the obstetrician if a score of 4 or above is calculated, as individual risk-benefit review is required.
items.stem: The SOP states that

options.text: LMWH may be given at any time after a regional anaesthetic block, provided the risk score is 2 or above.
a VTE risk score of 4 or above requires the prescribing midwife to alert an obstetrician for further review.
antiembolic stockings should be offered as a first-line alternative before pharmacological prophylaxis is considered.

items.explain: 핵심: a score of 4 or above requires individual obstetrician risk-benefit review.

items.extract:
Midwifery shift handover note (night to early):

Bay 3, Bed 2 — Ms Okonkwo, G2P1, day 1 post lower segment caesarean section. Estimated blood loss at operation 650 mL; two units packed red cells transfused intraoperatively. Haemoglobin at 06:00 this morning is 87 g/L; consultant notified, no further transfusion ordered at present — repeat FBC at 12:00. Wound dressing intact, no ooze, no erythema noted on morning check. Urinary catheter draining clear urine, output 45 mL/h overnight. Patient reports pain score 5/10 on movement; paracetamol and ibuprofen prescribed regularly but she has not received her 06:00 ibuprofen — please ensure this is given. LMWH due at 18:00 tonight; ensure stock is prescribed and available. Baby is with the mother in the room; latching observed at 04:00 feed and appeared adequate. Family visiting this afternoon; partner has been updated by night staff.
items.stem: The handover note requires the early shift to

options.text: request an urgent review of the haemoglobin result and arrange further transfusion before the ward round.
remove the urinary catheter and arrange a lactation referral for the mother's next feed.
administer the overdue ibuprofen dose and ensure the evening LMWH is prescribed and available.

items.explain: 핵심: administer overdue ibuprofen; ensure LMWH is prescribed and ready for 18:00.

gist: Part B = purpose of each extract; focus on verbs must/do not/ensure.
For CTG items, know that 'pathological' requires immediate escalation.
Check whether options reverse a must/must not or misquote a threshold.

sets.title: Mental health, capacity & consent extracts
sets.instruction: Six workplace extracts. Choose A, B or C. Focus phrases highlighted.

items.extract:
Memo from the ward consultant to all clinical staff:

Capacity is decision-specific and time-specific. Before you assume that a patient lacks capacity, apply the two-stage statutory test set out in the Mental Capacity Act 2005. First, establish whether there is an impairment or disturbance in the functioning of the mind or brain. Second, assess whether that impairment renders the patient unable to understand, retain, weigh up, or communicate the decision in question. Do not collapse these two stages into a general impression of 'confusion'. Each assessment must relate to the specific decision at hand — consent to a procedure is not the same assessment as capacity to refuse a medication. Document your findings the same day, including the decision in question, the evidence considered, and the conclusion reached. If you are uncertain, do not proceed on a best-interests basis without first consulting the senior medical or mental health team and, where appropriate, an independent mental capacity advocate. A blanket 'lacks capacity' notation on the admission clerking does not satisfy the legal requirement.
items.stem: The memo mainly tells staff to

options.text: complete a single capacity assessment at admission that covers all subsequent clinical decisions for that patient.
refer every capacity assessment to an independent mental capacity advocate before any best-interests decision is made.
apply the two-stage statutory test to each specific decision and record the findings on the day of assessment.

items.explain: 핵심: apply the two-stage statutory test to each specific decision and record the findings on the day of assessment.

items.extract:
Notice posted in the clinical area — acute psychiatric inpatient unit:

Any potential ligature point identified during a room search, patient observation, or routine inspection must be reported to the nurse in charge immediately and action taken to reduce or remove the risk before the shift ends. Do not defer removal to maintenance unless the point is structural and cannot be safely addressed at ward level. In that case, move the patient to a low-risk room while the referral is logged as urgent. Staff must not assume that a previously audited room remains safe; ligature risks can appear from everyday items including bedding, cords, and clothing. Document all identified risks on the environmental risk log and inform the on-call manager if a structural risk cannot be mitigated within the shift. The next shift team must be briefed at handover about any outstanding environmental risks that were not fully resolved.
items.stem: The purpose of this notice is to

options.text: remind staff that identified ligature points must be reported and mitigated before the shift ends, not deferred to the next day.
instruct staff to request a maintenance inspection at the start of every shift before any patient is admitted to a room.
inform nursing staff that all ligature-point audits and removals are the sole responsibility of the maintenance team.

items.explain: 핵심: identified ligature points must be reported and mitigated before the shift ends, not deferred to the next day.

items.extract:
Extract from the Trust rapid tranquillisation guideline (Section 4 — post-administration monitoring):

Following any administration of medication for rapid tranquillisation, the patient's pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, and oxygen saturation must be recorded every 15 minutes for the first hour, then every 30 minutes for the second hour, or more frequently if the clinical situation demands. Resuscitation equipment, including bag-valve-mask and emergency oxygen, must be immediately accessible in the clinical area throughout this period. If the patient becomes unresponsive, has an oxygen saturation below 90%, or the respiratory rate falls below 10 breaths per minute, call the resuscitation team immediately and do not administer further medication. Lorazepam and haloperidol should not routinely be combined without explicit senior medical authorisation, as the combination carries a heightened risk of respiratory and cardiovascular depression. Staff must document the clinical justification for rapid tranquillisation, the drug and dose given, and all monitoring observations in the patient's record.
items.stem: The guideline states that

options.text: combined lorazepam and haloperidol is the preferred first-line regimen whenever a patient is acutely agitated and cannot be de-escalated.
observations must be recorded at regular intervals after medication is given and resuscitation equipment must be immediately available throughout.
rapid tranquillisation may be administered by nursing staff acting alone whenever a senior doctor cannot be reached promptly on the ward.

items.explain: 핵심: observations must be recorded at regular intervals after medication is given and resuscitation equipment must be immediately available throughout.

items.extract:
Standard operating procedure — Section 5(2) of the Mental Health Act 1983:

Section 5(2) allows the registered medical practitioner or approved clinician currently responsible for an informal (voluntary) inpatient's treatment to detain that patient for up to 72 hours when they consider that an application for compulsory admission ought to be made. The power may only be invoked by the responsible clinician or their nominated deputy — it cannot be delegated to nursing staff. On completion of the relevant form (Form H1), the hospital managers' office must be notified within one hour and the Mental Health Act administrator informed. The 72-hour period begins at the time the form is signed, not from the time the patient was stopped from leaving. If, at the end of the 72-hour period, a full section has not been applied for and the patient wishes to leave, they must be allowed to do so unless alternative lawful authority exists. The patient must be informed of their rights under the holding power as soon as practicable after its invocation.
items.stem: According to the SOP, Section 5(2)

options.text: may be invoked by any registered nurse on the ward if a voluntary patient attempts to leave without medical staff being present.
detains the patient for a maximum of 24 hours while a formal Mental Health Act assessment is arranged by the clinical team.
may only be invoked by the responsible clinician or their deputy and provides a detention period of up to 72 hours.

items.explain: 핵심: may only be invoked by the responsible clinician or their deputy and provides a detention period of up to 72 hours.
focusPhrases: cannot be delegated to nursing staff

items.extract:
Extract from the observation and engagement policy — mental health inpatient services:

Observation level must be reviewed whenever there is a change in a patient's presentation, risk, or circumstances — including following any incident, significant disclosure, or change in leave status. The nurse in charge, in consultation with the responsible clinician where possible, must determine whether a higher or lower level is appropriate and document the rationale and time of change in the nursing record. A new observation level does not require a medical prescription but must be clinically justified and recorded at the time of change, not retrospectively. Continuous observation (one-to-one) may be initiated by a registered nurse in response to immediate risk, and the responsible clinician must be informed within one hour. Reductions in observation level should be agreed with the multidisciplinary team and are not solely at the discretion of the nurse in charge. Observation is a therapeutic engagement opportunity, not a purely supervisory task.
items.stem: The policy mainly requires staff to

options.text: review and adjust the observation level whenever a patient's risk or presentation changes, documenting the rationale at the time of change.
place every newly admitted patient on continuous one-to-one observation for a minimum of twenty-four hours before considering any reduction.
obtain written consultant approval before either increasing or decreasing the observation level of any inpatient on a section.

items.explain: 핵심: review and adjust the observation level whenever a patient's risk or presentation changes, documenting the rationale at the time of change.

items.extract:
Triage handover to liaison psychiatry — Emergency Department:

This is a 26-year-old woman who presented at 22:40 following a mixed overdose of paracetamol and diazepam, quantities unknown. Paracetamol level has been taken; result is still pending. She is medically stable at present but has not yet been assessed by the liaison psychiatry team. She has a known history of emotionally unstable personality disorder and two prior self-harm presentations in the last six months. She is distressed and intermittently refusing to engage with staff. She has explicitly stated she does not want her family contacted, and this wish must be respected unless the liaison team judges her to lack capacity or there is an immediate safety reason to override it. The treating physician has documented that a full mental state examination and risk assessment from liaison psychiatry are required before any decision regarding admission or discharge can be made. Please review within the hour.
items.stem: The note indicates that

options.text: the patient has already been assessed by the duty psychiatrist and is now waiting for a psychiatric inpatient bed to be allocated.
a full mental state examination and risk assessment from liaison psychiatry must be completed before any admission or discharge decision is made.
the patient has consented to information sharing with her family and the treating physician has documented this agreement in her notes.

items.explain: 핵심: a full mental state examination and risk assessment from liaison psychiatry must be completed before any admission or discharge decision is made.

gist: Part B = the main obligation or purpose of each extract; ignore incidental details.
Distractors often reverse a condition (unless / only / before) or misattribute a duty to the wrong person.
Watch for qualifying words such as 'immediately', 'at the time of change', and 'cannot be delegated' — they carry the correct answer.

신속 진정요법: 급성 흥분 상태에서 약물로 빠르게 진정시키는 처치

sets.title: Pharmacy, controlled drugs & prescribing extracts
sets.instruction: Six workplace extracts. Choose A, B or C. Focus phrases highlighted.

items.extract:
Memo from the pharmacy lead to all ward managers:

All controlled drug (CD) registers must have the running balance verified at every entry. The nurse who administers the drug signs in column A; the second signatory — who must physically witness the dose being drawn up and administered — signs in column B. The running balance is not a paperwork formality: it is the primary method by which stock discrepancies are detected without delay. If the calculated balance does not match what is held in the cupboard at any point, this must be reported immediately to the pharmacy lead and the site manager. Do not hold the report until the next routine ward check. Common sources of discrepancy include transcription errors and incorrect ampoule strength recorded. All discrepancies require an incident form regardless of whether diversion is suspected. Destruction of excess stock requires two authorised witnesses, at least one of whom must be a registered professional.
items.stem: The memo mainly tells ward managers to

options.text: ensure two registered nurses witness every controlled drug administration and countersign the drug destruction record.
submit the controlled drug register to pharmacy for monthly audit, noting any running balance errors found.
verify the running balance at each register entry and report any discrepancy to the pharmacy lead immediately.

items.explain: 핵심: verify the running balance at each register entry and report any discrepancy to the pharmacy lead immediately.

items.extract:
Extract from the Trust opioid conversion guideline (section 4):

When converting a patient from one strong opioid to another, calculate the equianalgesic dose using the Trust conversion table and then reduce the result by 25–30% to allow for incomplete cross-tolerance. This reduction is mandatory unless the patient's pain is inadequately controlled, in which case the reason for using a full equianalgesic dose must be clearly documented. For patients being converted from oral morphine to a transdermal preparation, the conversion must be undertaken by a prescriber with the appropriate competency, or in consultation with the pain or palliative care team. Do not use internet-based dose calculators as the sole reference for conversion ratios. Document the full calculation, the doses chosen, any rationale for deviating from the standard reduction, and a review date no later than 48 hours after commencement. If the patient is opioid-naïve, these conversion tables do not apply.
items.stem: The guideline states that when switching opioids, prescribers must

options.text: reduce the equianalgesic dose by 25–30% to allow for incomplete cross-tolerance, unless a documented reason exists.
use the full equianalgesic dose when converting between opioids, except when transitioning to a transdermal preparation.
refer every opioid conversion to the palliative care team and document their recommendation before prescribing commences.

items.explain: 핵심: reduce the equianalgesic dose by 25–30% to allow for incomplete cross-tolerance.

items.extract:
Notice to all prescribers from the antimicrobial pharmacist:

All patients receiving intravenous (IV) antibiotics must have a documented 72-hour review assessing suitability for IV-to-oral switch. Criteria for switch include: patient tolerating oral intake, temperature below 37.5°C for more than 24 hours, clinically improving, and an appropriate oral agent available with adequate tissue penetration. If a patient does not yet meet these criteria, the reason for continuing IV therapy must be recorded clearly on the electronic drug chart. Continuing IV antibiotics without a documented review is not acceptable under the Trust antimicrobial stewardship policy. The 72-hour clock starts from the time of the first IV dose, not from the time of admission. Monthly audits are conducted and omissions will be escalated to the prescribing consultant. For advice on suitable oral alternatives, contact the antimicrobial pharmacist on bleep 4471 or via the stewardship inbox.
items.stem: The notice requires prescribers to

options.text: switch all patients from IV to oral antibiotics within 72 hours of the first dose, regardless of whether clinical criteria are met.
review IV antibiotics at 72 hours against clinical criteria and document the reason if IV therapy is to continue.
contact the antimicrobial pharmacist for approval before prescribing any IV antibiotic course expected to run beyond 48 hours.

items.explain: 핵심: review IV antibiotics at 72 hours against clinical criteria and document the reason if IV therapy continues.

items.extract:
Extract from the Trust insulin prescribing standard operating procedure:

Prescribers must write the word 'units' in full when prescribing any insulin preparation. Never use the abbreviation 'U', 'IU', or any other shorthand, as these have been misread as zeros, resulting in tenfold dosing errors and serious patient harm. Similarly, write the full approved product name; do not abbreviate the formulation type or use informal product names. Insulin doses must be written as a numeral followed by the word 'units' with a clear space — for example, 12 units and not 12U. Before administration, a second trained member of staff must independently verify the prescription, the vial label, the graduated syringe markings, and the patient's identity. This two-person check is required for all routes of insulin administration, including subcutaneous, intramuscular, and intravenous. Do not pre-draw insulin into a syringe for administration at a later time. Any ambiguous prescription must be rewritten before it leaves the team.
items.stem: The SOP mainly instructs prescribers to

options.text: require a second trained staff member to countersign every insulin prescription before it is sent to pharmacy for dispensing.
avoid prescribing insulin preparations with a concentration above 100 units/mL unless specialist approval has been obtained.
write 'units' in full on all insulin prescriptions and never use the shorthand 'U' or 'IU' in place of units.

items.explain: 핵심: write 'units' in full on all insulin prescriptions and never use shorthand abbreviations such as 'U' or 'IU'.

items.extract:
Extract from the drug allergy and adverse drug reaction (ADR) documentation policy:

When a patient reports or experiences a possible reaction to a drug, the nature and severity of that reaction must be documented in detail. Writing only the word 'allergy' in the allergy field is insufficient: future prescribers need to know whether the reaction was anaphylaxis, urticaria, a gastrointestinal intolerance, or another recognised adverse effect, as this determines whether related compounds can safely be considered. The clinician who first identifies the reaction bears responsibility for documentation, even if the patient is subsequently transferred. Entries must be completed in the electronic prescribing record within two hours. Do not rely on a verbal account at handover; make the entry yourself. Reactions classified as 'intolerance' must include a description of the specific symptom experienced. Where the exact reaction is unknown, record what information is available and flag the entry for a structured allergy review at the next clinical opportunity.
items.stem: The policy requires clinicians to

options.text: withhold all drugs from the same class as a reported allergen until formal allergy testing has been arranged.
document the exact nature and severity of each drug reaction rather than recording only the word 'allergy' in the field.
refer every patient who reports a drug reaction to the specialist allergy clinic within two weeks of the event.

items.explain: 핵심: document the exact nature and severity of each drug reaction rather than recording only the word 'allergy'.

items.extract:
Out-of-hours pharmacy handover note (Thursday 20:45):

The urgent clozapine supply for ward 9B — 14-day stock, 100 mg tablets, pre-labelled — is currently in the dispensary fridge on shelf C. The night pharmacist must collect this before the main dispensary building is locked at 22:00; the porter cannot access the fridge once the shutters are secured. Lorazepam for ITU (four ampoules, signed out on CD requisition 447A) is already in the CD cabinet at the on-call desk. The ward pharmacist's bleep is now held by Dr Patel (bleep 2201) for clinical queries until 08:00. Unsigned insulin prescriptions for ward 6 are sitting on the printer and require a pharmacist signature before reaching the ward. A renal dose query is logged for Mr Hassan in bed 7: check the latest eGFR before advising the team. Near-expiry returns should go into the yellow returns tray on the dispensary counter, not into the fridge.
items.stem: The handover note indicates that the night pharmacist must

options.text: retrieve the pre-labelled clozapine supply from the dispensary fridge before the building is locked at 22:00.
contact Dr Patel on bleep 2201 to authorise the clozapine supply before collecting it from the dispensary fridge.
place near-expiry ward returns in the dispensary fridge for the morning pharmacist to assess and process.

items.explain: 핵심: retrieve the pre-labelled clozapine supply from the dispensary fridge before the building is locked at 22:00.

gist: Part B = identify the main purpose or single key instruction; watch for must / never / unless / before.
In pharmacy texts, distractors often assign the right action to the wrong person or the wrong deadline.
Focus phrases are verbatim clues — find them first, then re-read the surrounding sentence carefully.
