sets.title: Infection prevention & outbreak management extracts
sets.instruction: Six workplace extracts. Choose A, B or C. Focus phrases highlighted.

items.extract:
Memo from the Infection Prevention and Control team to all ward managers:

Two or more linked cases of acute vomiting and diarrhoea on the same bay constitute a suspected norovirus outbreak. Close affected bays to new admissions immediately; do not move patients between bays to fill gaps, as this will extend the outbreak. Cohort symptomatic patients and their contacts at bay level. All staff entering a closed area must wear a disposable apron and gloves; hand washing with soap and water is mandatory — alcohol gel alone is insufficient against norovirus. Enhanced cleaning with a chlorine-based solution (1,000 ppm available chlorine) is required at least twice daily and after every episode of vomiting or diarrhoea. Do not close the whole ward unless all bays are affected; partial closures allow unaffected areas to continue receiving patients. Notify IPC within one hour of declaring an outbreak. Only the IPC team can authorise reopening of a closed bay.
items.stem: The memo mainly tells staff to

options.text: close the entire ward immediately whenever two or more patients develop acute gastrointestinal symptoms.
transfer symptomatic patients to single rooms on another ward until stool specimens confirm norovirus.
close affected bays to new admissions and follow enhanced cleaning and contact precaution protocols.

items.explain: 핵심: Close affected bays to new admissions; enhanced cleaning and PPE (contact precautions) are required. Closing the whole ward is only if all bays are affected (rules out A); transfer to another ward is not mentioned (rules out B).

items.extract:
Notice from the IPC nurse to all clinical staff, posted at ward entrances:

Monthly unannounced hand hygiene compliance audits are now under way. Observers will assess all clinical staff against the WHO five moments for hand hygiene: before touching a patient, before a clean or aseptic procedure, after body-fluid exposure risk, after touching a patient, and after touching a patient's surroundings. Compliance below 80% will trigger an immediate debrief and mandatory re-training within five working days. Personal audit results are shared with line managers. Foam hand rub is available at every bed space and the ward entrance; however, when hands are visibly soiled or after contact with a patient with Clostridioides difficile or norovirus, soap and water must be used instead. Do not assume that wearing gloves removes the need for hand hygiene — gloves are not a substitute for the five moments protocol. All bank and agency staff are subject to the same requirements.
items.stem: The notice mainly tells staff to

options.text: follow the WHO five moments for hand hygiene or face mandatory re-training if compliance falls below 80%.
complete an online hand hygiene refresher module and pass an assessment before the next scheduled audit.
use soap and water exclusively for all patient contacts rather than the foam hand rub at the ward entrance.

items.explain: 핵심: five moments for hand hygiene; below 80% triggers mandatory re-training. No online module is mentioned (rules out B); soap and water is required only in specific situations, not for all contacts (rules out C).

items.extract:
Extract from the Trust MRSA admission screening policy (version 4):

All elective surgical patients must be screened for MRSA at the pre-assessment appointment, ideally 10–14 days before admission. A positive swab result requires decolonisation with mupirocin nasal ointment and chlorhexidine body wash for five days; elective surgery should be deferred until a clearance swab is negative. Emergency admissions are screened on arrival at the admitting ward; results are generally available within 24 hours. Patients with a previous MRSA-positive result are not automatically re-screened on every subsequent attendance; refer to IPC for an individual risk assessment if the interval since the last negative screen exceeds 12 months. Ward transfer documentation must record current MRSA status. Known MRSA-positive patients should be placed in a side room wherever possible; if no side room is available, notify IPC to agree a cohort arrangement before the patient is moved.
items.stem: According to the policy,

options.text: all patients, including emergency admissions, must be screened for MRSA at least ten days before any procedure.
elective surgery must be deferred until decolonisation is complete and a negative clearance swab has been obtained.
previously MRSA-positive patients must be placed in a side room and re-screened on every hospital attendance.

items.explain: 핵심: elective surgery should be deferred until a clearance swab is negative after decolonisation. The 10–14 days applies only to elective pre-assessment, not emergency admissions (rules out A); automatic re-screening on every attendance is explicitly not required (rules out C).

items.extract:
Extract from the Trust needlestick and sharps injury standard operating procedure:

In the event of a needlestick or sharps injury: immediately encourage the wound to bleed freely by squeezing gently; do not suck the wound. Wash thoroughly under running water with soap for at least 60 seconds; do not scrub with a brush or apply neat bleach to the skin. Cover with a waterproof dressing. Report to Occupational Health (during working hours) or the Emergency Department (outside working hours) without delay; HIV post-exposure prophylaxis must be started within one hour of a high-risk exposure to be most effective and cannot be given beyond 72 hours from exposure. Complete a Datix incident report the same working day. Preserve the source device in a secure sharps container if it is safe to do so; do not resheathe the needle under any circumstances. Inform your line manager. Most sharps injuries do not result in transmission of a bloodborne virus.
items.stem: The procedure requires staff to

options.text: complete a Datix incident report within 48 hours and arrange an Occupational Health appointment at the next available slot.
apply firm pressure and suck the wound to remove contaminated blood before washing it thoroughly under running water.
make the wound bleed, wash it under running water, and seek Occupational Health or Emergency Department review without delay.

items.explain: 핵심: encourage the wound to bleed, wash under running water, report without delay. Datix must be filed the same day (not within 48 hours) and OH should be attended immediately (rules out A); sucking the wound is explicitly prohibited (rules out B).

items.extract:
Extract from the Trust isolation priority guideline (Appendix 2):

When single-room availability is limited, the decision about which patient to isolate must be based on a risk assessment comparing transmission risk to others (the 'source' risk) against the patient's own vulnerability to infection (the 'sink' risk). A patient with suspected norovirus gastroenteritis and access to shared toilet facilities generally takes priority over an immunocompromised patient unless that patient is neutropenic and there is an active environmental mould risk. Patients with confirmed or suspected Clostridioides difficile, open pulmonary tuberculosis, or carbapenem-resistant organisms must always be escalated to IPC for same-day advice. Where no single room is available, cohorting patients with the same confirmed organism is the preferred alternative; mixing patients with different suspected pathogens in a single cohort bay is not acceptable. Staff must document the risk assessment outcome whenever appropriate isolation cannot be achieved. IPC helpline contact details are inside the back cover of every ward folder.
items.stem: The guideline states that

options.text: neutropenic patients must always be given priority over patients with diarrhoea whenever only one room is available.
single-room allocation must be guided by a risk assessment of which patient poses the greater transmission risk.
IPC must be contacted before any isolation decision is made, regardless of how urgent the clinical situation.

items.explain: 핵심: risk assessment comparing transmission risk to others determines priority. Neutropenic patients do not automatically take priority (rules out A); only specific high-risk organisms require same-day IPC escalation, not every decision (rules out C).

items.extract:
IPC handover note — C. difficile case, Bay 3, Bed 6:

Mr Okonkwo (62M) was confirmed CDI-positive this morning following three consecutive type 6–7 Bristol Stool Chart samples and a positive GDH/toxin assay. He has been moved to the single side room at the end of the bay. Oral vancomycin has been started; do not switch to metronidazole unless this has been discussed with microbiology. Side-room isolation must continue until the patient has been diarrhoea-free for at least 48 hours — do not discontinue isolation based on a negative repeat stool specimen alone. Soap and water only for hand hygiene in this room: alcohol gel does not eliminate C. difficile spores. Any ward transfers must be pre-notified to the receiving ward's IPC link nurse. A clinical review is due at 18:00 to reassess stool frequency and fluid balance. The Datix report has been opened; please add any updated clinical information before the night handover.
items.stem: The note indicates that

options.text: the patient must stay isolated with soap-and-water hand hygiene until he is diarrhoea-free for at least 48 hours.
the antibiotic should be switched from vancomycin to metronidazole once the first 24 hours of treatment have passed.
isolation can be discontinued as soon as a repeat stool specimen returns negative for C. difficile toxin.

items.explain: 핵심: diarrhoea-free for at least 48 hours before ending isolation; soap and water only. Switching to metronidazole is explicitly prohibited without microbiology discussion (rules out B); ending isolation on a negative specimen alone is explicitly prohibited (rules out C).

gist: Part B = purpose or main requirement of a workplace extract; watch must / do not / unless / until.

vocab.gloss: 탈집락화: 피부·비강의 MRSA 등을 항균제로 제거하는 처치
코호팅: 같은 병원체 감염 환자를 한 구역에 모아 격리
노출 후 예방 요법 (PEP): 혈액 노출 후 HIV 등 감염 예방을 위한 약물 투여
카바페넴 내성 균주 (CRO): 최후 항생제에 내성을 보이는 세균
C. difficile 글루타메이트 탈수소효소·독소 검사: CDI 확진에 사용

sets.title: Theatre, consent & surgical safety extracts
sets.instruction: Six workplace extracts. Choose A, B or C. Focus phrases highlighted.

items.extract:
Memo from the Theatre Safety Lead to all perioperative staff:

The WHO Surgical Safety Checklist is a mandatory patient safety requirement for every surgical procedure performed in this department, regardless of urgency or procedure length. The checklist has three stages: Sign In (before anaesthetic induction), Time Out (before surgical incision), and Sign Out (before the patient leaves the operating room). All three stages must be completed and recorded on the theatre documentation for every case. A completed checklist form must be filed in the patient's notes. No stage may be omitted or deferred because of time pressure or a surgeon's preference. If any stage is skipped, the senior scrub practitioner must document the omission and notify the theatre coordinator immediately. Completion of all three stages is the shared responsibility of the entire operating team, not solely the nursing staff.
items.stem: The memo mainly requires all perioperative staff to

options.text: complete only the stages that the operating surgeon considers necessary, omitting Sign Out when theatre time is limited.
delegate responsibility for completing all checklist stages to the senior scrub practitioner as the nominated team leader.
ensure all three checklist stages are completed and documented in the patient's notes for every surgical case.

items.explain: 핵심: 'All three stages must be completed and recorded … for every case' — 전체 세 단계를 빠짐없이 완료하고 기록해야 한다.

items.extract:
Extract from the Trust consent policy — patients who lack capacity:

When a patient aged 16 or over lacks capacity to consent to a procedure, clinical staff must follow the Mental Capacity Act 2005. Capacity should be assessed in relation to the specific decision and at the time the decision needs to be made; it is decision-specific and time-specific. If capacity is lacking, the team must identify who holds a valid Lasting Power of Attorney for health and welfare. Where no valid LPA exists, the clinical team must act in the patient's best interests, consulting family members or carers to understand previously expressed wishes. All decisions must be documented in full, including the views of those consulted and the reasons for the course of action chosen. Emergency procedures may proceed without delay under the principle of necessity, provided the intervention is the least restrictive option available.
items.stem: According to the policy, when a patient lacks capacity,

options.text: the clinical team must act in the patient's best interests, consulting relatives and fully documenting the decision.
the nearest family member holds legal authority to give or withhold consent on the patient's behalf.
the procedure must be postponed until an independent mental capacity advocate has provided a formal recommendation.

items.explain: 핵심: 'act in the patient's best interests, consulting family members' and 'all decisions must be documented in full' — 모든 결정은 최선의 이익 원칙에 따라 내리고 완전히 기록해야 한다.

items.extract:
Standard Operating Procedure — swab and instrument counts (operating theatres):

Swab and instrument counts must be conducted jointly by the scrub practitioner and the circulating nurse, using a read-aloud verbal confirmation technique. A baseline count must be performed before the procedure begins. A further count is mandatory before wound closure and again after wound closure is complete. If any discrepancy is found, the surgeon must be informed immediately and the wound must not be closed until the discrepancy is resolved, regardless of time pressure. Intraoperative imaging may assist in locating missing items but does not substitute for a full physical recount. The final count must be confirmed as correct by both practitioners, documented on the theatre record, and signed. Unresolved discrepancies must be escalated to the theatre coordinator and recorded as a clinical incident.
items.stem: The SOP requires that

options.text: the scrub practitioner conducts all counts independently and reports any discrepancy to the theatre coordinator after wound closure.
both the scrub practitioner and the circulating nurse must confirm counts jointly before and after wound closure.
a discrepancy in the swab count may be resolved by intraoperative imaging alone if the surgeon confirms the finding.

items.explain: 핵심: 'conducted jointly by the scrub practitioner and the circulating nurse' and 'before wound closure and again after wound closure' — 두 팀원이 공동으로 봉합 전후 계수를 확인해야 한다.

items.extract:
Notice to all surgical teams — site marking requirements:

Surgical site marking is mandatory for all procedures involving laterality, multiple levels, or multiple structures, and for any procedure where there is a realistic risk of wrong-site or wrong-patient surgery. Marking must be performed by the operating surgeon using a permanent skin marker before the patient is transferred to the theatre table. The mark must be placed directly over or adjacent to the intended incision site and must remain visible after skin preparation. Site marking must be completed in the anaesthetic room, before any sedation or general anaesthetic is administered, so that the patient can actively confirm the correct site. Marking by a trainee is acceptable only under the direct supervision of the responsible consultant. Do not use adhesive labels or any ink that may wash off during skin preparation.
items.stem: The notice states that surgical site marking

options.text: is required only for procedures with a laterality distinction and may be delegated to the surgical registrar in advance.
should be completed on the ward during the pre-operative nursing assessment and confirmed by the anaesthetist on arrival.
must be carried out by the operating surgeon in the anaesthetic room, before sedation or general anaesthesia is administered.

items.explain: 핵심: 'Marking must be performed by the operating surgeon' and 'completed in the anaesthetic room, before any sedation or general anaesthetic is administered' — 마킹은 집도의가 마취 전처치실에서 직접 시행해야 한다.
focusPhrases: before any sedation or general anaesthetic

items.extract:
Day Surgery Unit discharge criteria — guideline for nursing staff:

A patient may be discharged from the Day Surgery Unit only when all of the following clinical criteria are met: the patient is alert and orientated; vital signs have been stable for at least one hour; pain is controlled to a score of 3 or less on a 0–10 numerical scale using oral analgesia; nausea and vomiting are absent or mild; the wound site is clean and dry with no active bleeding; and the patient has passed urine. In addition, a responsible adult must be present to accompany the patient home and remain with them overnight. Discharge may not occur if the patient intends to travel alone or by public transport. The discharging nurse must complete and sign the discharge checklist and provide the patient with written post-operative instructions and emergency contact details.
items.stem: The guideline states that patients may be discharged from the Day Surgery Unit only when

options.text: all clinical criteria are met and a responsible adult is present to accompany them home and remain overnight.
the consultant surgeon has personally reviewed them and countersigned the discharge checklist before the patient leaves the unit.
pain has fully resolved and the patient has tolerated oral fluids without nausea for at least two hours.

items.explain: 핵심: 'all of the following clinical criteria are met' and 'a responsible adult must be present to accompany the patient home' — 임상 기준 모두 충족 및 보호자 동반이 함께 요구된다.

items.extract:
Post-anaesthetic recovery handover note — Theatre 3, 14:35:

Mr Choi, 58 years, ASA II, underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy under general anaesthesia (propofol/remifentanil/rocuronium, reversed with sugammadex). Procedure time 55 minutes; estimated blood loss <50 mL; no intraoperative complications. Currently in recovery bay 2 since 14:20. SpO₂ 97% on 2 L/min nasal oxygen; HR 78 bpm; BP 126/74 mmHg; temperature 36.6 °C. Pain score 6/10 despite 10 mg morphine IV intraoperatively and 1 g paracetamol IV. Ondansetron 4 mg given for postoperative nausea; no further episodes since 14:28. Anaesthetist Dr Patel contacted at 14:32 regarding ongoing pain management; awaiting review. Physiotherapy referral not indicated. His wife is present in the waiting area. Please do not transfer to the ward until Dr Patel has reviewed and analgesia is satisfactory.
items.stem: The handover note indicates that

options.text: the patient's vital signs are unstable and the anaesthetist has already been called to attend as an emergency.
the patient's pain is not yet adequately controlled and the anaesthetist has been asked to review him.
the anaesthetist has reviewed the patient and updated the analgesia plan, and he is ready for ward transfer.

items.explain: 핵심: 'Pain score 6/10 despite … morphine' and 'Anaesthetist Dr Patel contacted … awaiting review' — 통증 조절이 아직 불충분하며 마취과 의사의 검토를 기다리고 있다.

gist: Part B = what the extract mainly tells staff to do; focus on verbs must / do not / only when.
Theatre extracts often hinge on who is responsible and under what conditions an exception is permitted.
In consent questions, note that relatives do not hold automatic authority — the team must act in the patient's best interests.

vocab.gloss: 마취 유도: 전신마취를 시작하는 단계
지속적 위임장: 의사결정 능력 상실에 대비해 대리인을 법적으로 지정하는 문서
스크럽 간호사(실무자): 수술 중 무균 상태로 기구를 직접 다루는 수술팀원
측성: 수술 부위의 좌우 구분
스가마덱스: 로쿠로늄 등 신경근 차단제를 신속히 역전하는 약물

sets.title: Rehabilitation, discharge planning & community care extracts
sets.instruction: Six workplace extracts. Choose A, B or C. Focus phrases highlighted.

items.extract:
Memo from the physiotherapy lead to all ward physiotherapists:

Following the review of post-operative falls on Wards 6 and 7, we are updating the weight-bearing status documentation process with immediate effect. All weight-bearing orders must be transcribed onto the mobility board at the bedside within one hour of receipt. 'Partial weight-bearing' is not an acceptable entry; specify the permitted load in kilograms or as a percentage of body weight (e.g. 20 kg or 30%). Where the surgeon has not specified load, contact the operating team the same day rather than defaulting to non-weight-bearing. Patients must not be assisted to mobilise until the status is confirmed and documented. Physiotherapists handing over at shift change must verbally confirm the current order to the oncoming colleague; do not assume the board is always up to date. Any discrepancy must be escalated to the ward manager immediately.
items.stem: The memo mainly tells physiotherapists to

options.text: document a specific weight-bearing load and confirm the order verbally at handover.
contact the ward manager before mobilising any post-operative patient on Wards 6 and 7.
default to non-weight-bearing status whenever the surgeon has not provided written instructions.

items.explain: 핵심: specify load in kg or %; confirm verbally at handover. B overstates scope; C directly contradicts the instruction.

items.extract:
Extract from the community home oxygen assessment policy:

A home oxygen order form (HOOF) must be completed by a clinician with prescribing authority before any oxygen concentrator is installed in the patient's home. Ambulatory oxygen should be assessed separately from long-term oxygen therapy (LTOT); do not assume a patient assessed for LTOT automatically qualifies for ambulatory use. Qualifying criteria for LTOT require resting SaO₂ ≤ 92% on air on two occasions at least three weeks apart, when the patient is clinically stable. The fire safety checklist must be completed by the referring clinician, not delegated to the oxygen supplier. Smoking status must be documented; oxygen must not be commenced if there is an active smoker in the household unless a written safety plan is in place and the patient and all household members have been counselled. Home visits by the oxygen supplier do not replace the clinician's assessment.
items.stem: According to the policy, the fire safety checklist

options.text: may be delegated to the oxygen supplier to complete during the initial home installation visit.
must be completed by the clinician who is making the referral, not by the supplier.
is only required when there is an active smoker or unsupervised child living in the household.

items.explain: 핵심: fire safety checklist must be completed by the referring clinician, not delegated to the oxygen supplier.
focusPhrases: not delegated to the oxygen supplier

items.extract:
Pressure ulcer prevention notice — all clinical areas:

With immediate effect, all patients assessed as medium or high risk on the Waterlow scale must have a documented repositioning plan in place within four hours of admission. The plan must state the frequency of repositioning (minimum two-hourly for high-risk patients) and the equipment prescribed (e.g. alternating pressure mattress, heel protectors). Do not wait for a tissue viability nurse referral before starting basic preventive care. Referral to the tissue viability team is required for all patients who arrive with a pre-existing pressure ulcer of any grade or who develop a category 2 or above during their stay. Photographic documentation of existing skin damage must be taken at admission and repeated at 72-hour intervals. Staff must not reposition patients over, rather than off, bony prominences. Any new category 2 or above must be reported via Datix within 24 hours.
items.stem: The purpose of this notice is to

options.text: remind staff to await a tissue viability nurse referral before initiating any repositioning or equipment plan.
instruct staff to start preventive measures promptly and report new ulcers through the incident system.
require photographic documentation of all patients' skin on admission regardless of their Waterlow score.

items.explain: 핵심: start preventive care promptly (don't wait for TVN); report via Datix within 24 hours. A reverses the instruction; C overstates the photography requirement.

items.extract:
Community nursing referral SOP — district nursing team:

Referrals to the district nursing service must be submitted via the electronic referral system (ERS) and must include: diagnosis, current medications, wound care requirements if applicable, mobility status, next of kin contact details, and whether the patient has a keysafe or other access arrangement. Verbal referrals are not accepted except in genuine clinical emergencies, in which case a written ERS entry must follow within two hours. Discharge referrals must be received no later than 10:00 on the day of discharge to allow scheduling; referrals received after this time may result in a gap in care. The referring ward nurse is responsible for confirming that the patient has been informed a community nurse will visit. Do not give patients a specific appointment time; the team will contact them directly to arrange a suitable window. Ensure the GP has been notified of the referral at the point of submission.
items.stem: The SOP states that verbal referrals

options.text: are acceptable for all discharge referrals as long as a written ERS entry is completed before the patient leaves the ward.
are never acceptable under any circumstances and must in all cases be replaced immediately by an electronic ERS submission.
are only permitted in genuine clinical emergencies and must be followed by a written ERS entry within two hours.

items.explain: 핵심: verbal referrals accepted only in genuine emergencies; written ERS entry must follow within two hours.
focusPhrases: written ERS entry must follow within two hours

items.extract:
Extract from the care home discharge guideline:

Patients being discharged to a care home must not leave the ward until the receiving home has explicitly confirmed it can accept the patient on that date. Acceptance by phone alone is insufficient; written confirmation (email or secure message) must be on file before transport is arranged. The ward must supply the care home with a copy of the hospital discharge summary, current medication administration record (MAR), wound care plan, and the most recent nutritional assessment. Where the patient requires regular nursing procedures (e.g. PEG feeding, catheter care, syringe driver management), the ward nurse must contact the care home lead nurse directly to confirm staff competence. If competence cannot be confirmed, the discharge must be paused and the multidisciplinary team (MDT) notified. Do not document 'MDT agreed' on the discharge paperwork unless a formal MDT meeting or case conference has taken place.
items.stem: The guideline states that written confirmation from the care home

options.text: is only required when the patient needs regular nursing procedures such as PEG feeding or catheter care.
must be obtained and filed before transport to the care home is arranged.
replaces the need for the ward nurse to contact the care home lead nurse directly.

items.explain: 핵심: written confirmation must be on file before transport is arranged. A confuses confirmation with competence check; C contradicts the direct contact requirement.

items.extract:
Occupational therapy handover note — rehabilitation unit:

Mr Okonkwo (Bed 14) was reviewed today for home assessment planning. He is currently independent in transfers with a wheeled Zimmer frame on level surfaces but requires standby assistance on stairs. His home has seven steps to the front door with no handrail on the right-hand side; installation of a grab rail has been requested via the housing adaptation service, with estimated lead time of four to six weeks. Until adaptations are in place, ground-floor living arrangements have been discussed with the family and provisionally agreed. The patient has declined a stair lift assessment at this stage. He will need a commode and a perching stool; equipment has been ordered and delivery is expected within five working days. Discharge should not proceed until equipment is confirmed as delivered and the grab rail installation date is known. Please discuss the estimated discharge date with the consultant at tomorrow's ward round.
items.stem: The note indicates that Mr Okonkwo's discharge

options.text: should be deferred until the grab rail installation date is known and all ordered equipment has been delivered.
can proceed as soon as the family has confirmed the ground-floor living arrangement is suitable and agreed.
depends on the patient consenting to a formal stair lift assessment before he can leave the rehabilitation unit.

items.explain: 핵심: discharge should not proceed until equipment delivered and grab rail installation date is known.
focusPhrases: grab rail installation date is known

gist: Part B = identify the main instruction or purpose of each workplace extract.
Watch for negatives (must not, not accepted, do not wait) — distractors often reverse these.
Focus phrases are the key clause that directly answers the question.

장기 산소 요법 (Long-Term Oxygen Therapy)
욕창 위험도 평가 도구
